title: 2026-11-20 pi0.5 fine-tuning paired evaluation

protocol.task: left-arm grasp, lift >5 cm, and hold continuously >=0.6 s; no handover attempted

training.sampling: 4000 unique anchors sampled without replacement from the new 30-episode dataset
training.current_stage_dataset: only the 30 newly collected trajectories; prior 97+29 demonstrations are represented in initialization weights but were not mixed into this stage data loader

conclusion: The new 30-trajectory stage did not improve paired qualified grasp success: 5/18 versus 6/18 for the previous 5744-step checkpoint. Raw grasp success was 6/18 for each. This small development set is not a final generalization claim.
qualification: qualified success = physics-verified grasp success with no unintended contacts; audit_grasp_evaluations.py independently verifies the per-physics-step grasp evidence, but qualification also uses the saved contact audit.
limitations: All six evaluation layouts are development layouts; no final blind split was used.
No full handover, placement, reset, bimanual collaboration, or real-robot evaluation was run.
The 0.035 rad initial-offset demonstrations are not strict DAgger data collected from learner-induced deviations.
Synchronous evaluation pauses simulation during inference; wall-clock inference delay robustness was not measured.
Only 18 paired episodes; confidence intervals are broad and do not establish a meaningful model difference.
